focus: Windows: Git Bash resolution, paths with spaces, process-tree kill, PowerShell hooks

findings.title: TECH-SPEC claims process-tree kill uses a 'Windows Job Object' but v1 never built one — it shells out to taskkill /F /T /PID
findings.claim: ctx_execute ... kills the process tree (Windows Job Object) and bounds the whole handler incl. batch
findings.evidence: ARCHAEOLOGY: INTRODUCED_BY 9d1f44fb 'fix(executor): hide Windows console + drop .sh extension for shell exec (#384)' introduced Windows-specific kill handling; current code at cm-main src/executor.ts:196-200 is a comment 'Kill process tree — on Windows uses taskkill /T; on Unix kills the process group' followed by execSync(`taskkill /F /T /PID ${proc.pid}`, { stdio: 'pipe' }). Grep for 'JobObject' across all commits in cm-main returns zero hits. ORIGINAL_INTENT: the comment itself states the mechanism is taskkill /T, not a Win32 Job Object (CreateJobObject/AssignProcessToJobObject), which would require a native addon v1 never shipped. REGRESSION_RISK: if v2 is built to spec and someone actually tries to use a Job Object, that is new, unproven surface for v2 with no v1 track record (and no native-module policy decision on record); if instead the spec text is just wrong and v2 reuses taskkill /T, the doc misleads implementers/reviewers about what GP4's 'process tree killed' row actually tests. SAFE_FIX_CONSTRAINTS: either (a) correct the TECH-SPEC wording to 'taskkill /F /T /PID' to match the proven v1 mechanism and avoid introducing a native Job Object dependency with no npm (per the no-npm-for-v2 decision, a Job Object would likely need a native binding or FFI), or (b) if Job Object is a deliberate upgrade, add an ADR explaining why taskkill /T was insufficient and what GP4 evidence (issue #) motivates the change.
findings.fix: Change TECH-SPEC.md:437 to say 'taskkill /F /T /PID' (matching v1's proven mechanism) unless an ADR justifies switching to a real Job Object; either way, name the actual API so GP4's acceptance row is testable against a concrete mechanism.

findings.title: No spec coverage for PowerShell output encoding (BOM + console UTF-8 prelude) that v1 had to add to fix garbled Unicode paths/output
findings.claim: ctx_execute ... languages: shell, powershell, javascript, typescript, python, plus runtimes found on PATH (Q9)
findings.evidence: ARCHAEOLOGY: INTRODUCED_BY d0b4c987 'Fix PowerShell Unicode path handling' (src/executor.ts, +25/-2) in cm-main. ORIGINAL_INTENT (code comment / diff): added isPowerShellRuntime() detection, then on win32 with a PowerShell runtime, prepends a UTF-8 prelude ($OutputEncoding = [System.Text.UTF8Encoding]::new($false); [Console]::OutputEncoding = ...) and writes the script with a UTF-8 BOM via encodeShellScriptContent (\uFEFF prefix) — because default Windows PowerShell console/output encoding mangles non-ASCII paths and output otherwise. REGRESSION_RISK: TECH-SPEC lists 'powershell' as a supported ctx_execute language (Q9) but docs/v2 has zero mentions of BOM, OutputEncoding, or Unicode (grep confirmed no hits in TECH-SPEC.md or REVIEW-r4a.md). A naive v2 PowerShell runner re-breaks this exact v1 bug: non-ASCII paths (a HOME path with a space is already tested per ADR-0014's GP11 seed, but non-ASCII specifically is not) or non-ASCII output would silently corrupt. SAFE_FIX_CONSTRAINTS: v2's shell-language script writer must special-case the powershell/pwsh runtime the same way — UTF-8 BOM on the written script file and a console/output-encoding prelude — and GP4 or GP3 needs an explicit case asserting a non-ASCII string round-trips through a PowerShell-executed script.
findings.fix: Add a line to TECH-SPEC §ctx_execute (near line 437) requiring PowerShell/pwsh scripts to be written with a UTF-8 BOM and a console-encoding prelude, and add a GP4 test case with a non-ASCII string to assert it round-trips.

findings.title: No spec coverage for locale-independent Windows port-kill parsing used by ctx_doctor/ctx_upgrade cleanup
findings.claim: ADR-0010 describes doctor/upgrade port cleanup behavior but never mentions how the Windows port-owner lookup is parsed
findings.evidence: ARCHAEOLOGY: INTRODUCED_BY 1f70bee0 / 9ff53f78 'fix(ctx_insight): cap helper spawnSync + locale-independent Windows netstat parser (#469)', later reused by bd327123 'fix(server): route ctx_upgrade port cleanup through killProcessOnPort (#469 follow-up)'. ORIGINAL_INTENT (code comment at cm-main src/server.ts:4693-4701): netstat's STATE column is locale-translated (French 'À l'écoute', German 'ABHÖREN'), so the parser keys off the REMOTE column (wildcard 0.0.0.0:0 / [::]:0 for a listening socket) instead of STATE text, and this also fixed a prior bug where matching only the local port cross-matched a remote :port from an outbound connection and taskkill'd an unrelated process. REGRESSION_RISK: docs/v2/TECH-SPEC.md and ADR-0010 have zero hits for 'netstat', 'locale', or 'killProcessOnPort' (grep confirmed). If v2 reimplements doctor/upgrade's Windows port cleanup from scratch without this logic, it re-breaks both the non-English-Windows false negative and the wrong-process-killed bug from #469. SAFE_FIX_CONSTRAINTS: keep the REMOTE-column-based, locale-independent parse; add a doctor/upgrade golden test fixture with a non-English (e.g. French or German) netstat STATE string.
findings.fix: Add a line to ADR-0010 (or TECH-SPEC §3.9) stating the Windows port-owner lookup must parse netstat -ano by the locale-independent REMOTE-wildcard column, not the translated STATE column, and add a non-English-locale fixture to the doctor/upgrade golden tests.
